summary: Ephemeral namespace bind failures in ML CI causing resource access denied during model canary deploys
description:
Issue summary: Ephemeral GKE namespace creation succeeds but rolebindings fail intermittently during ML CI runs, leading to 'permissionDenied' errors when the canary deployment attempts to access GCS buckets and secret volumes.

Impact: Several CI-driven canary rollouts in staging have failed for the last 18 hours; developers cannot validate model rollouts and a few scheduled smoke tests are blocked. No production impact observed so far.

Environment: Staging cluster (k8s-ml-staging) in us-central1. CI runner uses workload-identity service account mapping to GCP service accounts. The failure appears tied to ephemeral namespace rolebinding automation that assigns iam.workloadIdentityUser and storage.objectViewer to the namespace SA.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger model canary CI (ci/canary-deploy with ephemeral-namespace flag).
2) CI creates namespace ns-ephemeral-<timestamp> and service account sa-ci-<id>.
3) Automation calls internal IAM binder to create RoleBinding and IAM policyBinding on the GCP service account.
4) Deployment pods mount secrets and attempt gsutil ls gs://model-artifacts-<staging>.

Observed behavior: RoleBinding creation API returns 200 but subsequent GCP IAM API responds with 403 permissionDenied when binding storage roles. Pod logs show accessDenied when reading secrets/GCS.

Expected behavior: Ephemeral namespace automation should complete rolebindings and GCP IAM policy updates within CI window so that pods can access required resources immediately.
logs:
Excerpt from CI run (timestamp 2026-03-12T14:22:03Z):
- binder: POST /namespaces/ns-ephemeral-16432/rolebindings 200 OK
- gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding model-ci-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role roles/storage.objectViewer -> ERROR: (gcloud.iam.service-accounts.add-iam-policy-binding) PERMISSION_DENIED: Caller does not have required permission iam.serviceAccounts.setIamPolicy

Kubernetes pod error (2026-03-12T14:22:41Z):
- error: failed to fetch secret redwood-gcs-creds: accessDenied: Access denied to secret manager resource projects/12345/secrets/redwood-gcs-creds
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: recent org-level constraint change or a condition on the GCP Organization's IAM Deny policies introduced a new guardrail that blocks service account policy changes from the CI service account. Checked Cloud Audit Logs for 'SetIamPolicy' and found DENY entries with policy name 'deny-unscoped-service-account-mods' starting 2026-03-12 13:50Z.

What we checked:
- Cloud Audit Logs: denied SetIamPolicy calls from CI service account with policy ref org-policy/deny-unscoped-service-account-mods.
- IAM Binder service logs: binder is authenticating as svc/ci-binder@infra.redwood.internal; binder has iam.serviceAccounts.setIamPolicy in its role historically.
- Recent Terraform change: infra/iam/org-policies.tf rolled out constraint to prevent unscoped service account IAM changes; PR merged 2026-03-12 by infra-ops (PR #5402).

Interim conclusion: Org policy now blocks binder's action unless call includes 'resource.name' matching a whitelist or has a precise principal. Binder calls are generic and therefore being denied.
comments: 2026-03-12 - Miguel Santos: Noticed a cluster of failures after infra PR #5402; creating this ticket to coordinate rollback or add exception for binder.

2026-03-12 - Priya Desai (Infra Ops): Confirmed PR #5402 enforced org policy to mitigate accidental broad SA perms. We can add an exception for svc/ci-binder but want to scope it to k8s-ml-staging only.

2026-03-13 - Security (Liam O'Connell): Need justification and timebound window for exception. Recommend temporary exception with audit logging and follow-up to change binder to use impersonation with precise principals.

2026-03-13 - Miguel Santos: Implemented emergency workaround: switched CI to pre-provision GCP policy bindings via infra-team-runbook job that runs under infra-admin account (audit logged). Rollouts resumed for two canaries successfully.
resolution_notes:
Workaround applied: Infra ops created a timebound, narrowly scoped exception to org-policy for the binder service account limited to projects 'redwood-staging-*' and service 'svc/ci-binder@infra.redwood.internal' until 2026-03-20. Additionally, CI was modified to call an infra-runbook job that performs bindings under infra-admin credentials for pending jobs.

Permanent fix plan:
- Modify binder to perform IAM operations using short-lived impersonated credentials that include the required 'resource.name' attribute resulting in allowed SetIamPolicy calls (owner: Miguel Santos, ETA 2026-03-19).
- Add integration test in ci-configs to validate org-policy-compliant binding flow (owner: Priya Desai, ETA 2026-03-18).
- Postmortem and documentation update to runbook and Confluence page (owner: Security team, ETA 2026-03-22).

Follow-ups created: INT-587000 to track binder code changes; INT-587001 for org-policy exception audit and removal on 2026-03-20.
next_steps: Add code change ticket for binder impersonation (INT-587000)
Update CI templates to include explicit project-scoping for policy binds
Schedule org-policy review with Security and Infra (invite sent)
